edition_label: OSCAR Plans, annual extracts of the November 2022 release (FY2017-18 to FY2021-22)
grain_description: Financial year x organisation x control budget detail x economic budget. The extract holds plans at organisation x sub-segment x economic category; I load and sum them to organisation x economic category and keep the control budget detail and economic budget. Nothing finer is comparable with outturn.
plan_basis: Resource and capital DEL (programme and administration), departmental AME, non-departmental AME and non-budget lines as OSCAR Plans. Resource DEL includes depreciation.
scotland_bga_rule: OSCAR carries the Scottish Government on one basis for plans and outturn, so a plan-to-outturn comparison within OSCAR needs no adjustment. The line is not on the basis of the Estimates or PESA tables and must not be compared with them (for FY2018-19 the Scottish Government resource DEL plan is 16.7bn against 16.7bn outturn in plan_oscar_totals.csv).
resource_basis_evidence: OSCAR Plans have no title; resource DEL here is OSCAR resource budget, which includes depreciation (docs/profiling/plan-sources.md section 13).
note: Descriptive columns are my reading of the published tables; the numbers themselves are never typed in here.

grain_description: Financial year x department group x measure (resource DEL excluding depreciation, capital DEL). One column of plans for the year of the workbook.
plan_basis: Resource DEL excluding depreciation and capital DEL, department groups with reserves and the Single Intelligence Account, as the workbook lists them.
scotland_bga_rule: The excluding-depreciation table carries Scotland at 35.3bn, against 27.0bn in the table including depreciation: the first is before the block grant adjustment, the second after it. Add nothing; compare with outturn that is also before the adjustment.
resource_basis_evidence: The sheet title says whether depreciation is in or out; the measure is read from the title.
note: The Scotland rule rests on magnitudes compared with PESA, which sql/tests/511 re-checks; I could not check it against the footnote text, which the reader does not keep.
